INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the key question of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. What is the price of food?
   B. How should we respond to instructions?
   C. How far is the market?
   D. Who is the tallest pupil?

2. In a singing game, who gives the instructions? (1 mark)
   A. The oldest pupil always
   B. The audience only
   C. Nobody
   D. The soloist

3. What does fluent reading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading very slowly word by word
   B. Reading in a whisper
   C. Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   D. Skipping words

4. Why should you underline new words in a text? (1 mark)
   A. To hide them
   B. To spoil the book
   C. To count pages
   D. So you can find their meanings and learn them

5. When copying a sentence, what should you check? (1 mark)
   A. Only the date
   B. Only the colour of the pen
   C. Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   D. Only the page number

6. A good comment during a gallery walk is (1 mark)
   A. This is ugly
   B. Nothing to say
   C. Your spacing is very even
   D. You cannot write

7. Where should letters sit in a lined book? (1 mark)
   A. Above the page
   B. Outside the margin
   C. Under the desk
   D. On the base line

8. Which instruction is clearer? (1 mark)
   A. Go and do it.
   B. Do the thing.
   C. Put it there.
   D. Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.

9. Which sentence uses a signal word for the last step? (1 mark)
   A. Then, wait.
   B. Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   C. First, wait.
   D. Next, wait.

10. What does reading with expression mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading without stopping
   B. Reading in a flat voice
   C. Reading in whispers
   D. Showing feeling in your voice as you read

11. Which feeling could a strong, fast voice show? (1 mark)
   A. Sleepiness
   B. Sadness
   C. Excitement
   D. Boredom

12. A sentence always begins with (1 mark)
   A. a capital letter
   B. a comma
   C. a number
   D. a full stop

13. Which is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Ending with a full stop
   B. Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   C. Using a comma in a list
   D. Starting a sentence with a capital

14. A comma is used to (1 mark)
   A. begin a sentence
   B. separate items in a list
   C. end a story
   D. show a question

15. Which question word asks about a place? (1 mark)
   A. Why
   B. Where
   C. When
   D. Who

16. Which question word asks about a person? (1 mark)
   A. Who
   B. Where
   C. How many
   D. When

17. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a conversation between two or more people
   B. a long poem
   C. a song
   D. a picture

18. Where can you check the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. In a bag
   B. On a shoe
   C. In a simple dictionary
   D. On a clock

19. What can you use to practise reordering sentences? (1 mark)
   A. A hammer
   B. Nothing
   C. A bucket
   D. Cut strips and arrange them

20. Which order is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Wash, go, wake up, eat
   B. Eat, go, wash, wake up
   C. Go to school, wake up, wash, eat
   D. Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three steps for building vocabulary from a text. (3 marks)

22. Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them. (3 marks)

23. Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters. (2 marks)

24. Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each. (5 marks)

25. Rewrite correctly: we live in nairobi (2 marks)

26. After listening to a safety story, describe how you would answer four kinds of comprehension questions and give one example of each. (5 marks)

27. Write a five-line role play dialogue on personal safety between a child and a stranger. Show the speaker names and use question marks correctly. (5 marks)

28. Read: The nurse bandaged the wound gently and the blood stopped. What does wound mean? Give two clues. (3 marks)

29. What is a verb? Give two examples. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — How should we respond to instructions?
   The lesson asks how we should respond to instructions in songs and games.

2. D — The soloist
   The soloist leads by singing the instructions and the group responds.

3. C — Reading smoothly without stopping at every word
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

4. D — So you can find their meanings and learn them
   Underlining marks the words to study.

5. C — Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   These are the points of neat copying.

6. C — Your spacing is very even
   Kind and specific comments help writers.

7. D — On the base line
   Letters rest on the base line.

8. D — Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
   It says what, where and why.

9. B — Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   Finally shows the last step.

10. D — Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   Expression shows the feelings in the text.

11. C — Excitement
   Excitement is often read faster and stronger.

12. A — a capital letter
   A capital letter shows the start of a sentence.

13. B — Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   A comma cannot join two complete sentences on its own.

14. B — separate items in a list
   Commas separate list items and show short pauses.

15. B — Where
   Where asks for the place.

16. A — Who
   Who asks about people.

17. A — a conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue records people speaking to each other.

18. C — In a simple dictionary
   Dictionaries give meanings.

19. D — Cut strips and arrange them
   Strips of sentences can be moved into order.

20. D — Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school
   This is the natural order of a morning routine.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible reason.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: We live in Nairobi.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capital letters and one for the full stop.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Answer who with a person (his mother), what with an event (touched the pot), where with a place (the clinic) and why with a reason (he wanted to see the steam). Give short, full answers and ask for repetition if needed.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each kind and example, and one mark for full sentences.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five correct lines, for example Child: Good afternoon. Stranger: Do you want a ride? Child: No, thank you. I will wait for my mother. Stranger: Are you sure? Child: Yes, I am telling my teacher.
   Working / marking points: One mark for speaker names, one for a safe message, one for correct questions and two for five clear lines.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wound is an injury. Clues are the nurse, bandaged and blood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and two marks for clues, awarding one for each up to two.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.
